skill.description: Frontend coding standards, Angular component patterns, and Tailwind design rules for the Guessimate UI.
skill.summary: Guides Angular and Tailwind frontend work for the Guessimate user interface.

security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, tables, and style-guide wording. The skill is documentation-only frontend guidance for Angular and Tailwind CSS, with no executable scripts, network behavior, file access, or prompt injection attempts found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use **Standalone Components** (`standalone: true` is default in v19+).
Prefer the `inject()` function over constructor injection for better type inference and cleaner code
- **Reactive Data:** Use `computed()` for derived state and `effect()` sparingly for side effects.
We use **Tailwind CSS 4** with a semantic color palette defined in `styles.css`.
2. **No Magic Numbers:** Use theme values (e.g., `p-4` not `p-[16px]`).
3. **Dark Mode:** Use the `dark:` modifier for all color-related classes.
Colors are defined using CSS variables in the `@theme` block:
- Avoid external CSS files; use **Tailwind CSS** utility classes directly in the template.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent Angular component structure and visual styling across the Guessimate UI. This skill provides practical standards for components, state, Tailwind CSS usage, colors, cards, and typography.
actual_capabilities: Describes the Angular 20, Tailwind CSS 4, Signals, RxJS, and Angular CLI frontend stack.
Defines a feature-based directory structure for core, layout, features, websocket, and shared code.
Guides standalone component structure, inline templates, explicit imports, and Angular control flow usage.
Explains local and shared state patterns using signals, computed values, effects, and service stores.
Documents semantic Tailwind color names, dark mode rules, card styling, dividers, and header typography.
limitations: It is tailored to the Guessimate Angular frontend and may not fit unrelated products without adaptation.
It provides conventions and examples, but it does not validate or modify source files automatically.
It covers selected component and style patterns, not a complete design system token reference.
It assumes Angular 20+ and Tailwind CSS 4 conventions.

use_cases.title: Build Consistent Components
use_cases.description: Apply the project rules for standalone components, inline templates, imports, selectors, and Angular control flow.

use_cases.title: Review UI Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check whether new UI code follows the project structure, state management rules, naming conventions, and Tailwind styling standards.

use_cases.title: Align Product UI Decisions
use_cases.description: Use the documented colors, card treatments, typography, and dark mode rules when planning or refining interface changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Angular component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular component against the ui-style-guide. Focus on naming, standalone component structure, inline template usage, and Tailwind classes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-style-guide to propose a feature-based folder layout for this new UI feature. Include components, pages, services, and models where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Refine State Management
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve how state is represented in a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this feature state design with the ui-style-guide. Recommend where to use signals, computed values, effects, RxJS, and service stores.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a UI Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across structure, state, and visual consistency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this UI flow against the ui-style-guide. Cover project structure, component boundaries, state handling, semantic colors, dark mode, cards, and typography.

output_examples.input: Review a new session page component for style-guide alignment.
output: The component follows the standalone pattern and uses explicit imports.
Move feature state into a session store because multiple child components consume it.
Replace arbitrary spacing with theme spacing and add dark mode classes for color utilities.

output_examples.input: Plan folders for a lobby management feature.
output: Place routed containers under the feature pages area.
Keep presentational lobby widgets under feature components.
Use a feature service for lobby state and keep shared UI helpers in the shared area.

output_examples.input: Improve a card layout for visual consistency.
output: Use the documented surface background, border, and divider treatment.
Keep the standard rounded corner size for cards and containers.
Use the header typography pattern for title and subtitle text.

best_practices: Use the guide before writing new Angular UI code, not only during review.
Keep feature-specific logic inside feature folders and reserve shared code for reusable utilities.
Apply semantic color names and dark mode variants consistently for every color-related class.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unrelated feature code into technical folders only by file type.
Do not add arbitrary Tailwind values when a project theme value exists.
Do not rely on constructor injection when the guide recommends the inject function for the component.

faq.question: What frontend stack does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Angular 20+, Tailwind CSS 4, Angular Signals, RxJS, and Angular CLI with Esbuild.

faq.question: Can this skill generate complete UI code?
faq.answer: It can guide UI code generation, but it is primarily a standards reference for structure, state, and styling.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands or modify files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown style guide and does not include executable scripts or automation.

faq.question: Is it useful outside the Guessimate project?
faq.answer: Yes, but some guidance is project-specific and should be adapted before use in another product.

faq.question: How should reviewers use it?
faq.answer: Reviewers can compare pull requests against the documented component, state, structure, color, and typography rules.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: It does not provide detailed accessibility rules, so teams should pair it with their accessibility checklist.
